subject.title: [Bug] PTY silently disabled in sandbox mode without warning when pty:true is set

question: For explicit `pty: true` in sandboxed exec, should OpenClaw warn and continue without PTY, or reject the tool call?
rationale: The source issue is clear, but choosing warning-only versus fail-closed changes how a sandbox capability denial is surfaced to users.

options.title: Warn And Continue
options.body: Emit a clear warning while preserving the current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

options.title: Fail Explicit PTY
options.body: Reject sandboxed exec calls that explicitly request PTY so the user must choose another execution mode.

options.title: Adopt Fork PR After Decision
options.body: Use the open fork PR only after maintainers choose the warning semantics and require current proof.

recommendation.title: Warn And Continue
recommendation.body: Emit a clear warning while preserving the current sandboxed non-PTY execution behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across exec PTY support, fallback behavior, and docs.
